key_highlights: Wall Street enters correction territory with heavy tech/AI sell-offs, setting up the ASX for immediate downward pressure following a $169B weekly loss.
Domestic credit conditions tighten further as five cumulative RBA rate hikes severely erode borrowing power, accelerating Sydney housing price drops.
Consumer discretionary enters distress, highlighted by David Jones cutting ~1,700 staff while competitor Myer captures market share.
Australian dollar faces significant depreciation pressure alongside heightened recession warnings and softening labour market dynamics.

sectors.trend: Severe correction driven by global AI valuation unwind, enterprise hiring freezes, and legislative digital duty-of-care requirements.
sectors.implications: High valuation multiples for ASX tech (e.g., WTC.AX, XRO.AX) face severe derating; capital raising shifts toward niche, cash-generative plays.

sectors.trend: Mounting mortgage distress and accelerating property price declines challenge retail bank balance sheets following cumulative rate hikes.
sectors.implications: Major banks (CBA.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX) face net interest margin contraction, decelerating credit growth, and rising bad debt provisioning.

sectors.trend: Severe consumer retrenchment leads to retail restructuring, department store staff downsizing, and shifting spending patterns.
sectors.implications: David Jones retrenchments highlight structural margin compression, directly benefiting Myer (MYR.AX) via customer and supplier capture.

sectors.trend: Resilience in precious metals restarts, rare earth technological breakthroughs, and offshore expansion counter broad equity weakness.
sectors.implications: Capital rotating selectively into gold producers (e.g., NST.AX, EVN.AX) and critical minerals developers while base metals remain macro-sensitive.

sectors.trend: Scrutiny on major transition projects like Snowy Hydro 2.0 alongside geopolitical positioning in regional oil and gas assets.
sectors.implications: Traditional energy producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX) offer defensive cash yields as domestic transition delays and import reliance raise supply concerns.

key_themes: Global equity correction contagion impacting ASX benchmarks (^AXJO, ^AORD)
RBA monetary policy transmission straining household balance sheets and housing valuations
Macro-driven divergence between defensive hard assets (gold, energy) and cyclical growth/tech

risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight high-PE growth tech equities; increase exposure to defensive cash-flow generators.
Reduce exposure to retail-heavy banks and residential REITs; prioritize diversified corporate credit.
Hold unhedged offshore earnings and USD-denominated commodity producers.
Avoid leveraged discretionary retail; favor consumer staples (WOW.AX, COL.AX).

opportunities.rationale: Gold restarts and safe-haven flows provide robust downside protection against market corrections and AUD weakness.

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical Long on Department Store Consolidation
opportunities.rationale: Myer gains market share, supplier leverage, and customer footfall from David Jones closures and mass layoffs.

opportunities.recommendation: Selective Critical Minerals & Rare Earths Exposure
opportunities.rationale: Metallurgical breakthroughs and commercial recovery milestones present high-conviction alpha independent of macro headwinds.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge Core Equities via Index Overlay
defensive_moves.rationale: Protect portfolio capital following a $169B market loss and impending Wall Street spillover.
Severe borrowing capacity erosion and falling Sydney home prices raise loan book impairment risks.

market_outlook.short_term: Volatile and bearish over the next 1–3 months as the ASX digests global tech corrections, local retail distress, and housing valuation declines.
market_outlook.long_term: Subdued growth over 6–12 months with potential stagflation or recession risks looming into 2027, favoring disciplined miners and low-gearing defensive yield.
key_catalysts: RBA monetary policy statements and commentary on policy overtightening
Australian quarterly GDP and CPI releases evaluating recession probabilities
Wall Street AI sector stabilization and NASDAQ technical support levels
Domestic retail sales prints and employment data post-restructuring waves
watch_list: AUD/USD exchange rate approaching key cyclical supports
Sydney and Melbourne property auction clearance rates and median price trends
Major bank net interest margins and 90+ day mortgage arrears rates
Iron ore 62% Fe CFR and spot gold price trajectory
